column1: #notes label(bedroom_cell_v1_notes) orientation and edge roles
This file is one tileable bedroom cell; not a placed room. It carries no
coordinates and no fort-specific anchor; a caller supplies the anchor
when applying it: quickfort run bedroom-cell-v1.csv -c X Y Z.
Grid orientation; 5 columns by 5 rows; row 1 is the top (north) edge as
displayed below:
- column 1 (all rows): west seam edge; shared with a neighbour cell
tiled to the west. Do not re-designate this column's wall if a
neighbour cell already owns it.
- column 5 (all rows): east seam edge; same rule; shared with a
neighbour cell tiled to the east.
- row 1; columns 2-4: north edge; this cell's own; never shared.
- row 5; columns 2-4: south edge; the entrance edge. Column 3 of row 5
is the entrance gap: open floor; no wall; no door. Columns 2 and 4 of
row 5 are this cell's own wall; not shared (the entrance edge is not
a seam; nothing tiles against it; a corridor does).
- rows 2-4; columns 2-4: the 3x3 interior.
Every s cell below is a finished-wall intent; not a material. This
concrete file resolves that intent as smooth (s; #dig mode) because it
assumes the wall tile is standing natural rock; the common case for a
freshly carved room. A tile that is not standing rock (most likely a
seam edge where the neighbour cell's own dig already removed the
material there) resolves instead as a constructed wall (Cw; #build
mode) at the same coordinate. See blueprints/README.md; Resolving the
wall intent; before applying this template somewhere that assumption
may not hold.
